# 4 Ezra Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — The narrow gate and fate of souls

---

**1** When I finished speaking, the angel sent to me on the previous nights was sent again.

**2** He said: Get up, Ezra. Listen. I have come to speak to you.

**3** I said: Go ahead. He said: Imagine a sea laid out in a vast, open expanse — deep and enormous —

**4** but with an entrance like a river, a narrow channel.

**5** If someone wants to reach the sea — whether to see it or sail it — how do they get to the open water without first passing through the narrow part?

**6** Or think of a city built in a wide open plain, packed with everything good you could want,

**7** but whose only entrance is on a steep cliff, with fire on one side and a deep pool on the other,

**8** and between the two there is only a single thin path, so narrow that only one person can walk it at a time.

**9** If this city is promised to someone as their inheritance, how do they receive it unless they walk that dangerous path first?

**10** I said: That's right, my lord. He said: And that is exactly Israel's situation.

**11** I made the world for Israel's sake. When Adam broke my statutes, what I had made was put under judgment.

**12** The entrances of this world were made narrow, painful, and exhausting — few and miserable, riddled with dangers, loaded with hardships.

**13** But the entrances of the greater world are wide and safe, and they yield the fruit of immortality.

**14** Unless the living pass through the difficult and frustrating things of this life, they can never receive what is stored up for them.

**15** So why are you distressed, when you know you are mortal? Why are you shaken, knowing you are corruptible?

**16** Why are you not thinking about what is ahead rather than what is in front of you now?

**17** I said: O LORD, my lord — you have declared in your law that the righteous will inherit these things and the wicked will perish.

**18** So the righteous must endure the narrow way, hoping for the wide open beyond; while those who lived wickedly have suffered the narrow path and will never see the wide.

**19** He said: You are not God's superior, and you are not wiser than the Most High.

**20** Let many of the living perish rather than that the law of God set before them should go unheeded.

**21** For God gave firm instructions to everyone who came into the world — what to do to live, what to avoid to escape punishment.

**22** They refused to obey. They argued back. They invented empty theories,

**23** cooked up wicked deceptions, and some of them even said the Most High does not exist. They ignored his ways completely.

**24** They treated his law with contempt, threw out his covenants, refused to honour his statutes, and never did what he required of them.

**25** So, Ezra: the empty get emptiness; the full get fullness.

**26** For the time is coming — when the signs I told you about arrive — and the bride will appear. She who has been withdrawn from the earth will come out into the open.

**27** And anyone delivered from the evils I described will witness my wonders.

**28** For my son the Messiah will be revealed together with those who are with him, and he will bring joy to those who survive for four hundred years.

**29** And after those years my son the Messiah will die — and so will every human being alive.

**30** The world will lapse into primeval silence for seven days, as at the first beginning, so that no one at all remains.

**31** After seven days the dormant age will wake up. Everything corruptible will perish.

**32** The earth will hand over those sleeping in it. The dust will give back those resting silently within it. The storehouses will return the souls entrusted to them.

**33** The Most High will appear on the judgment seat. Misery will end. Long-suffering will be over.

**34** Only judgment will remain. Truth will stand firm. Faithfulness will grow strong.

**35** Reward will follow. The prize will be revealed. Righteous deeds will rise up. Unrighteous deeds will not be allowed to sleep.

**36** The pit of torment will come into view; opposite it, the place of rest. The furnace of Gehenna will be revealed; opposite it, the paradise of delight.

**37** Then the Most High will say to the nations raised from the dead: Look — and understand. This is what you denied. This is what you refused to serve. These are the commandments you despised.

**38** Look before you now: on one side, delight and rest; on the other, fire and torture. That is what he will say to them on the day of judgment.

**39** There has never been a day like that day and there never will be — it will be like a day of absolute battle.

**40** That day will have no sun, no moon, no stars,

**41** no clouds, no thunder, no lightning, no wind, no water, no air, no darkness, no evening, no morning,

**42** no summer, no spring, no heat, no winter, no frost, no cold, no hail, no rain, no dew,

**43** no noon, no night, no dawn, no glow, no brightness, no light at all — except the blazing glory of the Most High, by which everyone will see what has been assigned to them.

**44** It will last roughly a week of years.

**45** This is my judgment and its appointed process. I have revealed it to you alone.

**46** I answered: O LORD — I said it before, and I say it again: blessed are those who are alive and keep your commandments.

**47** But what about those I prayed for? Who among the living has not sinned? Who born of woman has not broken your covenant?

**48** And now I can see it: the world to come will bring delight to few and torment to many.

**49** Because an evil heart grew up inside us, and it has pushed us away from these good things, dragged us into corruption and into the roads that lead to death, showed us paths of destruction, and taken us far from life. Not just a few of us — nearly everyone ever created.

**50** He answered: Listen, Ezra. I will teach you. I will give you one more warning.

**51** This is exactly why the Most High did not create one world but two.

**52** You say the righteous are few and the wicked are many. Here is why that is not the problem you think it is.

**53** If you have only a few precious stones, do you add lead and clay to make up the number?

**54** I said: Lord, of course not.

**55** He said: Exactly. Now go and ask the earth directly — approach it gently and it will tell you.

**56** Say to it: You produce gold and silver and copper, as well as iron and lead and clay.

**57** But there is more silver than gold, more copper than silver, more iron than copper, more lead than iron, more clay than lead.

**58** So which is more precious and desirable — the common or the rare?

**59** I said: O LORD who rules over us — the rare is more precious.

**60** He said: Think through your own answer; for the person who possesses something hard to find rejoices far more than the one who has plenty.

**61** And that is exactly how my promised judgment will work; I will rejoice over the few who are saved, because they are the ones who gave my glory its victory and through whom my name was honored.

**62** And I will not grieve over the multitude of those who perish; for they have become like vapor, like flame and smoke — ignited, blazing briefly, then gone.

**63** I cried out: O earth, what have you produced? If the mind is made from the same dust as everything else,

**64** it would have been better if the dust had never been born, so the mind would never have been born from it, and the mind would not now be driving us into torment.

**65** I genuinely do not know which is better — sorrow or joy.

**66** He answered: Understand this: it is better for the creature to enter judgment having sinned than to pass through life free of sin and never face judgment at all.

**67** I said: I know, O LORD, that the Most High is called merciful — because he has mercy on those who have not yet come into the world,

**68** and on those who turn away from his law,

**69** and in his patience and compassion he is called merciful forever and ever.

**70** For if he were not merciful, the world could not continue to exist, and the uncountable people who have sinned could not go on living.

**71** He answered: The Most High made this world for the sake of many, but the world to come for the sake of few.

**72** Here is the comparison again, Ezra: ask the earth — it gives more common clay for making pots than it gives rare dust that yields gold. And so it is in this present world.

**73** Let me add one more thing. Don't talk about the Most High too freely,

**74** and don't poke too eagerly into your own present condition — have you forgotten what judgment means for someone found lacking?

**75** Don't celebrate yourself too much, but don't torment yourself too much either.

**76** On the day of judgment each person will be judged according to their deeds.

**77** I said: What happens to those who are gathered? How are they divided?

**78** He answered: Here is how it works. The souls of the righteous leave the dwelling place of the corruptible and will never return to it.

**79** But the souls of the wicked will be allowed to see the dwelling place of those who are saved — and they will also see the torment that awaits them.

**80** So this is what happens: they wait through seven days of rest, and when those seven days are up, they begin to ache with longing for the places they have left behind.

**81** This is the order of experience for those who kept the way of the Most High once they are separated from their mortal bodies.

**82** While they were still alive in those bodies, they worked hard and served the Most High tirelessly, facing danger every hour so that the law-giver's design might be fulfilled in them.

**83** And here is what they experience:

**84** First of all, they see with immense joy the glory of the one who receives them — and they rest in seven stages.

**85** First stage: they fought strenuously against the evil impulse planted within them, refusing to let it drag them from life into death.

**86** Second stage: they watch the wandering of the souls of the wicked and the punishment coming toward them.

**87** Third stage: they see the testimony that their Creator bears on their behalf — that they lived their lives keeping the law given to them in trust.

**88** Fourth stage: they comprehend the rest they now enjoy — gathered in their chambers, guarded by angels in deep stillness — and they see the glory awaiting them at the last.

**89** Fifth stage: they rejoice at having escaped corruption and secured the inheritance to come, and they look back at the narrow, punishing road through which they traveled to reach such greatness and blessedness.

**90** Sixth stage: it is revealed to them that their faces will shine like the sun, and they will become like the brilliance of stars — incorruptible from that moment on.

**91** Seventh stage — which surpasses all the others: they exult fearlessly. They are bold without shame. They rejoice without anxiety. They are rushing toward the face of the one they served in life — and they are about to receive their reward in glory.

**92** That is the order of the righteous souls, as now announced. And the paths of torment described are what awaits those who refused to listen.

**93** I said: Will souls actually be given time after separating from their bodies to see all the things you have described?

**94** He said: They will have seven days of freedom. During those seven days they will see what I have told you, and afterward they will be gathered to their appointed places.

**95** I said: If I have any grace before you, show me one more thing — will the righteous be able on the day of judgment to intercede for the wicked or plead with the Most High on their behalf:

**96** fathers for children, children for parents, brothers for brothers, relatives for kinsmen, friends for their dearest friends?

**97** He answered: Since you have found grace before me, I will show you this too. The day of judgment is decisive and stamps the seal of truth on everything.

**98** Just as it is now — a father doesn't get sick or sleep or eat or be healed instead of his son, nor a son instead of his father, nor a master instead of his slave, nor a friend instead of his dearest friend —

**99** so on that day no one will pray for another, no one will carry another's load; because on that day each person carries only their own righteousness and their own wickedness.

**100** I said: But wait — how is it that Abraham prayed for the people of Sodom, and Moses prayed for our ancestors who sinned in the wilderness,

**101** and Joshua after him interceded for Israel in the time of Achan,

**102** and Samuel and David prayed during the plague, and Solomon prayed for those in the sanctuary,

**103** and Elijah prayed for those who needed rain, and prayed for the dead to come back to life,

**104** and Hezekiah prayed for the people during Sennacherib's invasion, and so many others prayed for so many?

**105** If the righteous were able to pray for the wicked during this present life — when corruption is rampant and wickedness is everywhere — why couldn't they do it in the future?

**106** He answered: This present world has not reached its end. The fullness of glory has not yet come to live in it. That is why the strong were allowed to pray for the weak.

**107** But the day of judgment will be the end of this present time and the beginning of the immortal age to come — when corruption will be over,

**108** intemperance gone, unfaithfulness abolished, righteousness flourishing, faithfulness established.

**109** When that day comes, no one will be able to show mercy to someone condemned in judgment, or harm someone who has been vindicated.

**110** I said: This is my conclusion — first and last: it would have been better if the earth had never produced Adam. Or else, having produced him, should have stopped him from sinning.

**111** Because what is the point of everyone living in misery now and facing punishment after death?

**112** O Adam — what have you done? You sinned, but the consequences were not yours alone; they fall on all of us who descended from you.

**113** What good is it that we have been promised immortal life, when the things we have done deserve death?

**114** What good is an eternal hope held out to us, when we in our wretchedness come to a wretched end?

**115** What good are safe and healthy dwelling places prepared for us, when the way we lived was wicked?

**116** What good is the glory of the Most High to protect the pure, when we have walked in utter wickedness?

**117** What good is paradise revealed with its undying fruit and its healing abundance, if we will never enter it

**118** because we walked in bad places?

**119** What good is it that the faces of the self-controlled will shine brighter than the stars, when our own faces will be darker than the dark?

**120** We never thought during our lifetimes, while sinning, that we would have to pay for it after death.

**121** He answered: This is the whole point of the contest that every person born on earth is engaged in:

**122** those who lose will suffer what you described; those who win will receive what I described.

**123** For this is the way Moses spoke about to the people while he was alive: Choose life, that you may live.

**124** But they did not believe him, or the prophets who came after him, or even me speaking directly to them —

**125** so their greatest grief will not be the torment itself, but the fact that they abandoned the Most High, despised his law, and turned away from his ways.

**126** And those who now dwell in the saved places will not mourn for those who perish — they will rejoice, because their own full number is now complete. The torment of those henceforth preserved is finished, while the glory of those now vindicated can never diminish.

**127** He said: When God decided to save Israel and bring them to himself, he did not call on one Egyptian to take pity on them —

**128** he sent signs and wonders to pull them out of Egypt and bring them through a terrible road to safety.

**129** I will do the same for those who are alive at the end. I will not mourn the many who perish.

**130** Because they too were given freedom, and they threw it away — they despised the Most High, scorned his law, and abandoned his ways.

**131** And they crushed his righteous people underfoot.

**132** They told themselves: There is no God — even while knowing full well that they were going to die.

**133** Just as the good things described will receive you, so thirst and torment that have been prepared will receive them. The Most High never wanted human beings to be destroyed.

**134** But the human being who was created defiled the name of his Maker and was ungrateful to the one who gave him life.

**135** And so my judgment is now imminent.

**136** I have not revealed these things to everyone, only to you and a very few others like you.

**137** I said: O LORD, you have shown me a great many signs that you will perform in the last time, but you have not told me when.

**138** He answered: Keep careful track of time in your mind. When you see that a portion of the signs I announced has already come to pass,

**139** then you will understand that the exact moment has arrived when the Most High is about to visit the world he made.

**140** So when you see earthquakes among peoples, disorder among nations, conspiracies among kings, confusion among leaders, panic among princes — then understand, and at that moment recognize: these are the very words the Most High spoke to you.
